summary: 100-foot tower at the Texas Forestry Museum in Lufkin, Angelina County; built 1936; sources disagree on whether it came from East River or near Conroe.

access.note: Museum exhibits are open to visitors, but Bowman says the tower has been altered to keep climbers off

events.note: Texas Highways says the tower was built in 1936; Bowman says towers like it were built by the Civilian Conservation Corps in 1936
A 1974 newspaper item said a 100-foot tower would be built on the proposed museum site and stay Texas Forest Service property
Bowman says the Lufkin tower was moved from its site near Conroe in 1976. The FFLA lists East River, Harris County, as its origin. The origin is disputed.

notes_for_editor: Origin is disputed and not settled. FFLA lists East River, Harris County (gone); Texas Highways and Bowman say the tower came from near Conroe. The 1974 newspaper item speaks of a tower to be built on the museum site, not of a move. Bowman's 1976 move date is the only move date found. The Texas Forestry Museum website returned no text when fetched, and the Lufkin Daily News tower article returned HTTP 429 and was not read; the museum's own history may settle the origin. Record county, coordinates and status match the FFLA list. The 100-foot height is from press and writeup descriptions; the overall height and whether it is the original cab are not confirmed. Agency is from the 1974 notice of intended ownership, not a current source. Bowman's column is dated February 28, 2010 and was updated December 6, 2012, so the access and climbing status is only as recent as that update.
